abilities.name: Ring-A-Ding-Ding! Hexhunter Chime
abilities.description:
Determined to take down the "evil" witch and save her beloved Descartes, Prune unleashes the power of the wind! She strikes at the Witchlure Bell using her Banehunter Oathhammer, dealing Anemo DMG.
If Prune triggers a Swirl or Stellar Swirl reaction in the opponent with this attack, her Ring-A-Ding-Ding! Hexhunter Chime is changed to Clang Clang! Witch-tribution Comes! for the next 6s.

Clang Clang! Witch-tribution Comes!
Ensconces the **Banehunter Oathhammer** in the element involved in the earlier Swirl or Stellar Swirl reaction. After tapping to unleash, Prune will launch a midair kick at the Banehunter Oathhammer, dealing DMG to opponents in front of her of the corresponding elemental type.
abilities.caveat: The Tolling Rally team buff is shown after every skill hit; in game only the element-converted hammer, available for 6s after a Swirl, grants it.
_curatorNotes: [superseded 2026-09-15 — gcsim shipped him] No gcsim source and no verified frame data — character stays frameless (FRAMELESS_EXEMPT). Skill CD 15s confirmed against sidecar. The Clang Clang conversion (204.6%→485.8% @T10 vs base 167.4%→397.7%) is a conditional alternate Press unlocked by a prior Swirl; not modelled as a separate AbilityVariant because the distinction is only decision-relevant with frame timing, which is unavailable. Base skill also generates 5 Anemo particles on first hit (KQM quickguide).

[A7] The converted follow-up form is 'Clang Clang! Witch-tribution Comes!'; the base cast and the converted form aren't modeled as separate variants because there is no verified frame data source for their hit timing (already in _curatorNotes).

↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "Not modeled: the stronger element-converted form gained for 6s after triggering Swirl, or its hit timing. That converted hit is what powers the team DMG buff (Tolling Rally)."

abilities.name: The Bell Tolls! The Hunt Is On!
abilities.description:
Prune gently swings the Witchlure Bell, dealing Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. After this, the Bell will enter the Hunter-Seeker mode.

Witchlure Bell: Hunter-Seeker
In this mode, the Witchlure Bell will follow the current active character, attacking surrounding opponents at intervals and dealing AoE Anemo DMG. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG.

passives.name: Verdict and Punishment

_curatorNotes: A1 follow-up: during the Burst, when the Hunter-Seeker Witchlure Bell's hit triggers a Swirl, a Banehunter Oathhammer strikes for 150% ATK in the swirled element (Burst DMG). Trigger authored as a self Swirl during an active summon (the Bell). Element omitted — it matches the Swirl's converted element (pyro/hydro/cryo/electro), which is enemy-aura dependent and not fixed. ↻ procCooldown: 1.2 AUTHORED 2026-09-16 (T0.5) — the note above's "No stated ICD in kit text; none authored" is superseded by the source. gcsim asc.go:50-53 holds a1SwirlCheckICDKey for 1.2s and it is SHARED across all four swirl elements, so the hammer cannot answer two swirls of different elements inside the window. ⛔ Still not authorable: gcsim also narrows the trigger to `atk.Info.Abil == "Witchlure Bell"` (asc.go:46), i.e. only the BELL's swirls count, where ours fires off any swirl Prune triggers during any active summon of hers. passives.description: During the Elemental Burst **The Bell Tolls! The Hunt Is On!**, after the Witchlure Bell in Hunter-Seeker mode deals DMG to an opponent, if this DMG triggers Swirl or Stellar Swirl in an opponent, it will also summon a **Banehunter Oathhammer** that will deal 150% of Prune's ATK as DMG to them, with the DMG Type matching the Elemental Conversion from the Swirl or Stellar Swirl. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG.

passives.name: Tolling Synchronicity

_curatorNotes: A4 Tolling Rally: nearby party members EXCEPT Prune gain a DMG Bonus (applies to Normal/Charged/Plunge/Skill/Burst DMG) for 5s after Prune hits with a converted (Elemental Conversion) Banehunter Oathhammer — i.e. the Clang Clang skill or the A1 Burst hammers. Scaling: +0.025% per point of Prune's ATK above 2,000, capped at +50% (needs 4,000 ATK). Modelled as allDmgBonus with an 'unknown' value because the BuffValue scaling form cannot express the 2,000-ATK threshold offset; the exact bonus is Prune-ATK-dependent and not planner-resolvable. Value snapshots Prune's ATK at grant time but applies as a dynamic DMG% window on the recipient, so snapshottable:false. Trigger anchored to onHit skill (the converted Clang Clang hammer) as the representative source; A1 Burst hammers also grant it (can't be jointly expressed in one trigger). This is Prune's headline team-support function.

passives.caveat: With 2+ Hexerei in the party, team reactions also grant ATK; that is shown on every team reaction, though in game only Hexerei teammates carrying Tolling Rally count.
passives.description: After Prune hits an opponent with the **Banehunter Oathhammer** that has undergone Elemental Conversion, other nearby party members will gain the Tolling Rally effect for 5s: When Normal, Charged, or Plunging Attacks, or Elemental Skills and Bursts deal DMG to opponents, that attack's DMG will be increased based on the portion of Prune's ATK in excess of 2,000 when they become affected by the Tolling Rally effect. Every excess ATK point increases that instance of DMG by 0.025%, up to a total of 50% max.
_curatorNotes: 2026-08-15: the unknown-value `description` is a DISPLAY LABEL — the tooltip renders it verbatim in the value slot — and this one was authored as a 182-char sentence, three to seven times the corpus norm (25-43 chars) and the only one that wrapped the tooltip to a full-width paragraph (⚓ Nate spotted it). Shortened to Arlecchino's register ('+1% per 100 ATK above 1000, cap 20%' — the identical threshold shape) and Ineffa's habit of naming the holder ('+2.5% per 100 ATK Ineffa has'). Naming Prune in the label is what retires the dropped clause: the buff scales off HIS ATK, and 'per 100 of Prune's ATK' says so without a caveat. Underlying rate, unchanged: 0.025% DMG per single ATK point above 2,000 = 2.5% per 100, reaching the +50% cap at 4,000 ATK. ⛔ Not a caveat — the style guide reserves those for the timeline visibly diverging from the game, and 'never explain how the kit works'.

constellations.description:
During the Elemental Burst **The Bell Tolls! The Hunt Is On!**, when the Witchlure Bell is in Hunter-Seeker mode, Prune gains the Hunt the Witch effect: Prune's ATK increases by 10%, and when the Witchlure Bell and the **Banehunter Oathhammer** that has undergone Elemental Conversion hits an opponent, it further increases her ATK by 5%. _curatorNotes: ↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "During the burst, her ATK rises by 10%, then a further 5% each time the Witchlure Bell or a converted Banehunter Oathhammer hits, up to 40%. Shown at the 10% starting value."

↻ THE WINDOW IS 13.55s, AND 17.55s AT C6 — 2026-09-16 (T0.5), where it was a flat 12 at every level. gcsim burst.go:26-52 computes `duration = 813 + c6BurstBonusDur()` (that bonus is 4*60) and then adds the status at frame 57 for `duration − 57`, so the mod ENDS at 813f = 13.55s at C0–C5 and 1053f = 17.55s at C6. Measured before: `Prune Q` at C6 drew the C2 bar 7.88→19.88s against a bell bar running to 23.88s — visibly mismatched, since the C6 +4s reached only the summon.

⚓ And the LENGTH is the right number here, not the end time, because the anchor already agrees: a cast's buff window starts at `fieldStart`, which is the summon's `summonActivatesAt` — 57 — and 57 is exactly gcsim's `burstStatusDelay`. So 756f (12.6s) and 996f (16.6s) land the ends on gcsim's 813f and 1053f to the frame. ⚠️ Measured, not assumed: an earlier draft authored the END times and drew 0.95→18.50s. Two mutually-exclusive `constellation` arms because `constellationScaling` reads only a gainStacks amount and a tick cap, never a duration.

factionBonuses.name: Secret Rite
factionBonuses.description: With 2+ Hexerei members in the team, a Hexerei teammate carrying Tolling Rally who triggers an Elemental Reaction grants Prune +60% ATK for 5s; if that reaction is a Swirl, the character who triggered it also gains +30% ATK for 5s.

_curatorNotes: Hexerei Secret Rite (Witchseeker's Vow, Luna VII). Wiki talent text: "After a Hexerei character in the party affected by the Tolling Rally effect triggers an Elemental Reaction on an opponent, Prune's ATK is increased by 60% for 5s." Source: Fandom 'Witchseeker's Vow' (pageid 457454), fetched 2026-07-29; no gcsim source exists for Prune. Two runtime gates are not expressible as Condition leaves and are NOT modeled: the triggering party member must themselves be Hexerei, and must be carrying Tolling Rally (A4). Trigger authored onReaction any/team; the count gate rides the teamFaction condition.

Second half of the same rite: "If the Elemental Reaction triggered is a Swirl Reaction, the triggering character's ATK will additionally be increased by 30% for 5s." (Fandom pageid 457454, fetched 2026-07-29). This is additive on top of the +60% self buff, which fires on any reaction. Target authored as 'active' — there is no 'triggering character' target in the schema; the swirl trigger is nearly always the on-field character, so 'active' is the honest approximation. Same unmodeled gates as the self buff (triggerer must be Hexerei and carry Tolling Rally). Swirl authored as the four element-specific swirl reactions per the retired-'swirl'-key convention.

[superseded 2026-09-15 — gcsim main has Prune (#2712)] Stages 1-3 effects-only curation 2026-07-14 (no gcsim source, no open PR — frames impossible; stays FRAMELESS_EXEMPT). Mechanics sourced from KQM quickguide + KQM TCL library + genshinguides + official talent text (genshin-db). CD/energy/duration cross-checked against docs/curation/talents/prune.json (all PASS). Team-facing capabilities: A4 Tolling Rally (team allDmgBonus, Prune-ATK-scaled), C6 flat ATK (self+active), burst Witchlure Bell (off-field summon). Known gap: bell tick cadence unverifiable → off-field DMG under-claimed (see burst _curatorNotes).

Hexerei layer added 2026-07-29 (Luna VII): factions=['hexerei'] + Secret Rite from the Witch's Eve Rite passive 'Witchseeker's Vow'. Sole evidence is the Fandom wiki talent infobox (pageid 457454, MediaWiki API fetch) — Prune has no gcsim implementation, so no source backstop exists for these values. No permanent (ungated) kit patch found: the rite text describes only the two count-gated ATK buffs, and the Prune page's talent/constellation text shows no revised values, so no regular kit structure was touched.

↻ 7.0 (genshin-db 5.2.13, 2026-08-31): kit text rewritten from "Swirl" to "Swirl or Stellar Swirl", so `stellarSwirl` joins the trigger. ⚓ Needed because a Stellar Swirl enabler (Sandrone/Odette/Cryo Traveler) REPLACES every Cryo Swirl party-wide — without this the effect would go dark in those teams. ⛔ Only added where HoYo actually renamed the text: a buff on the base reaction is NOT a buff on the converted one, so characters whose text was left alone (Venti, Lohen) stay as-is.

AUTHORED 2026-08-31: "every excess ATK point [above 2,000] increases that instance of DMG by 0.025%, up to a total of 50% max" = 2.5% per 100 ATK. ⚓ ratio is VALUE PER 100 STAT UNITS (BuffValue JSDoc: contribution = (ratio/100) × stat), which is why a "per 1% ER" kit reads as ratio 40, not 0.4. Was an `unknown` placeholder pending `offset`.
